page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8488C cores running at 3.2 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for machine learning acceleration. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2055.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 33.32 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Passmark CPU score of 12373.16 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 8098.75. Memory performance represents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is high at 684.22 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is weak, and uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 50.44 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 10.68 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 14.29 GB/sec.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the presence of Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, this instance is configured for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It is suitable for web serving, software compilation, and light machine learning inference, as demonstrated by a prompt processing speed of 58.59 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. However, text generation on larger models is limited, with the 7B model achieving only 7.8 tokens per second. The lack of bundled local storage requires external network-attached storage for persistent data. The flex-class designation provides a cost-efficient entry point for compute-intensive workloads that can tolerate baseline network limits and moderate memory bandwidth.
